steps.say: This lesson follows the start of the system, from the bootloader to the first program. A **bootloader** is the small program the firmware runs first. Its job is to load the kernel into memory and start it.
The bootloader is Limine, and this is its whole setup. It loads the kernel and two **modules**, files handed to the kernel in memory: the base system (base.cpio) and the OS's own files (initrd.cpio).
A `cmdline:` line gives the kernel words at start. This one connects an AI on a real PC. `verbose` and `netlog` are others the kernel looks for.

steps.anchor: /* ---- the big files, read by the kernel itself ----
steps.through: * UEFI (a real computer, from a USB stick the kernel can't read yet) the files come whole, as before. */
steps.say: `${FW_TYPE}` in limine.conf picks a folder by firmware. With BIOS (the VMs) the bootloader loads only a small placeholder, and the kernel reads the big file from the disc itself, which is much faster.
`kmain` is where the kernel begins. It sets up memory, interrupts and the other processor cores, then starts a thread to run `init_main`. The boot thread becomes the first core's idle loop.

steps.through: usb_init(); /* drivers/usb: keyboards, mice, sticks (its own thread: nothing waits for it) */
steps.say: `init_main` runs the kernel's self-tests, starts the clock and the file system layer, then finds devices: PCI, the screen, input and USB.
The disks come next, before anything is unpacked, because the base system may have to be read from the disc by the kernel.
The archives are unpacked into ramfs, a file system in memory. The base system goes first (the Freedesktop Platform as /usr), then the OS's own files over it.

Then the model file is placed. `preload_state_from_fwcfg` is a development aid: a VM can hand in a mind and a design through fw_cfg, so tests skip onboarding. The command line's AI settings are read last.
Last, "OS BOOT OK" is printed (the tests wait for that line) and the first program, /sbin/init, starts.
init becomes process 1. Its first three open files, input, output and errors, are all the console.
init is told OS_MODE. A test can ask for a mode through fw_cfg, otherwise it is "interactive", a normal start.
/sbin/init is userland/init, put into the initrd when the image is built.
Next: **03 The kernel's core**, the parts kmain just set up.
